stem: Suresh invests Rs 50,000 today at 8% per annum compounded annually for 3 years. What is the future value at the end of 3 years? [Use: (1.08)³ = 1.2597]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student rounds 1.2597 to 1.24 and computes 50,000 × 1.24 = 62,000, rounding the given factor prematurely.
Student uses 1.26 instead of the given 1.2597, computing 50,000 × 1.26 = 63,000.
Student computes simple interest only: 50,000 + 3 × 50,000 × 0.08 = 62,000, then further rounds to 60,000, mixing up formulas.

explanation: Future value = P × (1 + r)^n. With P = 50,000, r = 0.08, n = 3: FV = 50,000 × 1.2597 = Rs 62,985. Using the given factor exactly is essential; rounding 1.2597 changes the answer.

explanation_sections.punchline: Rs 50,000 multiplied by the given factor 1.2597 equals Rs 62,985. Using any rounded version of the factor leads to a wrong option.
explanation_sections.approach: Write FV = P times (1 + r)^n. The stem provides the exact value of (1.08)^3 to use. Multiply the principal by that factor without rounding it. Always use the factor the stem gives you, not an approximation you compute in your head.
explanation_sections.lesson: When the stem provides a computed power, use that exact value. Rounding the factor is the trap that produces the nearby wrong options in future-value questions.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Reject option (1) instantly: Rs 60,000 would be simple interest for only two years at 8% on Rs 50,000. Multiply 50,000 by 1.2597 directly, keeping all four decimal places.
